title: security: RBAC v2 KMS region pinning + audit logging hardening
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Harden RBAC v2 by enforcing KMS region pinning and improving audit logging. Includes control-plane validation, migration script for existing customer KMS bindings, docs, and an opt-in rollout behind feature flag. No behavior change for customers without KMS region constraints.
description: Motivation: customers in regulated industries require strict data residency guarantees tied to KMS keys. This PR hardens RBAC v2 and the KMS integration by adding enforceable region-pinning checks and richer audit events so compliance teams can prove key residency. Summary: 1) Add region pinning validation to RBAC v2 policy evaluator (control plane + private installer), 2) Record structured audit entries when KMS bindings are created/updated/used (includes previous_region/new_region and decision_reason), 3) Migration tool to surface existing KMS bindings that violate new residency constraints and optionally auto-remediate behind a feature flag, 4) Docs and Linear/Jira links, 5) E2E and unit tests across runtime and installer. Checklist: - [x] Policy validator and unit tests - [x] Audit event schema and logging hooks - [x] Migration script + dry-run mode - [x] Private installer validations + upgrade note - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] QA run in staging and Dedicated cluster rollout plan Rollout plan: feature gated behind `rbac_v2_kms_region_enforce` config. Default mode is `audit` which logs violations but does not block; after 2 weeks of monitoring and fixes we flip to `enforce` for customers who opted in via tenant config. Related: ENG-8452 (Linear), SUP-9241 (Jira).

feat(audit): structured audit events for kms binding changes

test: add unit + e2e tests for kms residency enforcement
docs: document region pinning and migration process

pkg/rbac/v2/policy_validator_test.go — unit tests for new cases

review_comments: Maya Thompson: Please add a safety net for customers during initial rollout — prefer audit mode by default and require explicit opt-in for enforcement. Also expand the migration dry-run output with sample remediation commands.
Avery Chen: Addressed — feature defaults to 'audit' and migration now prints suggested remediation CLI commands. Added notes to docs. PTAL.
Diego Rivera: Found a race in installer preflight where KMS bindings are checked before tenant config is loaded; added suggestion to defer check until after config sync.
Avery Chen: Fixed by moving preflight check after sync and added a unit test that simulates delayed config sync.
ci_checks: integration tests: flaky on first run (timeout in kms emulator) — rerun
notes_on_backward_compatibility: Default behavior is non-breaking: enforcement is opt-in and the system logs audit events when running in audit mode. Migration tool supports dry-run only unless explicit --apply flag is provided.
merge_details: Merged by Maya Thompson via squash merge. Commit message summarized the feature, included migration instructions and rollout plan. Changelog entry added under vNext.
discussion_summary: Team agreed on audit-first rollout, explicit tenant opt-in for enforcement, and shipping improved audit events for compliance reporting. Operations to run migration in staging and notify customers with KMS bindings out-of-policy before enforcement.
testing_and_qa: Manual QA performed on staging with a Dedicated cluster; migration dry-run produced expected remediation suggestions. Added unit tests for policy evaluator and e2e test covering create/update KMS binding paths. No regressions found in unrelated RBAC tests.
support_plan: Customer success to notify tenants flagged by migration dry-run. Support playbook added to docs with steps to temporarily opt-out customers and guidance for on-prem operators (private installer).
security_considerations: Audit events redact tenant-sensitive fields but include KMS key IDs and region metadata. KMS key IDs are hashed in some outputs to avoid leaking full identifiers in low-priv logs. All changes reviewed by Security (SEC-312).
how_to_revert: Revert is a single commit revert on main to remove the policy validator checks and audit hooks; migration changes are additive and safe to keep. Operators can set `rbac_v2_kms_region_enforce=false` to disable enforcement immediately.
